known.title: Finished-plan step guard tests the current status instead of the target
known.description: setStepStatus refuses a finished plan's step change when `!terminal(current)` instead of `!terminal(target)`. A finished plan can no longer move a planned or in-flight step to done or skipped (the terminal repair that the contract's 'Steps after the landing merge' section and the refusal list require, e.g. marking a post-merge deploy step done), and it now lets a done or skipped step move to planned or in-flight, because the second guard is skipped for finished plans. The new regression test only checks in-flight -> in-flight, which both conditions refuse, so it does not catch this.

known.title: Generic spawn-error branch shadows the ENOBUFS branch
known.description: runGh checks `if (result.error)` before `result.error?.code === 'ENOBUFS'`, so the overflow branch is unreachable. Output above the 256 MiB buffer is reported as `gh <cmd> <sub> failed: spawnSync gh ENOBUFS` instead of the documented `gh <argv[0]> <argv[1]> output exceeded 256 MiB` string that the plan names as a new helper string. No test exercises the overflow, so the gate stays green.

known.title: Large-output regression test stays below Node's 1 MiB default maxBuffer
known.description: The #68 regression case writes 20 comments of 50,000 characters, about 1,000,000 bytes plus roughly 5 KB of JSON overhead. That is less than spawnSync's default maxBuffer of 1,048,576 bytes, so the test passes without the new maxBuffer and does not guard #68. The plan's Step 1 says the test must send more than 1 MiB of output.

known.title: Review-diff recipe word-splits untracked file names
known.description: The code-review recipe iterates `for file in $(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)`. Unquoted command substitution splits paths on whitespace and expands glob characters, and ls-files without -z C-quotes unusual names. Untracked files with spaces, glob characters, or non-ASCII names are split, expanded to other files, or passed as nonexistent paths. `git diff --no-index` then fails, and the next paragraph tells the manager that nonzero exits are expected, so those files silently drop out of the complete-candidate review diff.

known.title: Linked-branch steps check out the branch before the clean-checkout gate
known.description: The Linked branch procedure now runs `gh issue develop ... --checkout` (step 2) before `git status --porcelain` (step 3). Ambient uncommitted work is carried onto the linked plan branch before the dirty check can block or request a separate worktree. This contradicts the rule that ambient work is never moved and the previous requirement that the checkout be clean before `gh issue develop --checkout`. Step 5's 'if a call fails, list again' is now also separated from the gh calls it covers.

known.title: Contract says bracketed severity counts only at line start; the helper counts it anywhere
known.description: The canonical review-record rules say that a code pass becomes fixes-required only when a line starts with `[critical]` or `[high]`, and that a bracketed marker inside finding prose does not count. severeFinding() in plan.mjs matches `[critical]`/`[high]` anywhere on the line, and the new tests rely on that (`1. Bug [critical] src/example.mjs:1 ...` -> fixes-required), as does the plan's Research. Reviewers and managers who follow the contract will mispredict which comments block a pass.
